patch_description: A fundamentally different two-stage approach. (1) Replication: instead of the sequential greedy "replicate argmax(w/cnt)" loop, use a fully vectorized water-filling solver: a batched binary search over the load threshold t, where each logical expert i gets ceil(w_i/t) replicas (clamped to >=1), followed by an exact residual fixup that hands leftover replica slots to the experts with the largest w/cnt. This directly minimizes the maximum per-replica load w_i/cnt_i (the quantity that drives expert balancedness), and the physical layout is then built with a single batched `searchsorted` instead of r sequential scatter steps. (2) GPU packing: LPT greedy for the initial assignment, then a stronger pairwise-swap local search that, for the most-loaded GPU, evaluates swaps against *every* other GPU (not just the least-loaded one), choosing the item/partner pair that minimizes the resulting maximum load. Packing cardinality is preserved by swaps, and loads are updated incrementally so each round is O(P·k) vectorized ops. Both stages are batched across all layers/nodes, giving both better balance and much lower runtime than the per-item Python loops of the reference implementation.
